slides.headline: She can save his life with one ribbon.
slides.sub: John Everett Millais, A Huguenot, on St. Bartholomew's Day, 1852

slides.headline: Paris, August 1572
slides.text: Paris, 24 August 1572. Catholic mobs are about to hunt down the Protestants, the Huguenots. Thousands will be dead by morning.

slides.headline: Two lovers
slides.text: Behind a garden wall, two lovers meet in secret. She is Catholic. He is a Huguenot. And she knows what is coming.

slides.headline: Her plea
slides.text: Look at her face, lifted up to his. She is begging him, because she has found a way to save him.

slides.headline: The white band
slides.text: The order says every good Catholic must tie a strip of white linen round his arm. She is tying it on him.

slides.headline: His answer
slides.text: But look at his hand. While he holds her close, he is quietly pulling the band away. He will not pretend.

slides.headline: His choice
slides.text: He looks at her calmly. His mind is made up. To wear it would mean denying his faith, even to stay alive.

slides.headline: The garden
slides.text: At the edge of the wall grow Canterbury bells, often a sign of faith and constancy. Millais painted every brick of this wall from life.

slides.headline: Love or faith
slides.text: About 3,000 people died in Paris that day. Millais never tells us his fate. Would you have worn the ribbon?
